newsitem.title: USA: ConEd N.Y. nuke moves into cold shutdown.
newsitem.headline: ConEd N.Y. nuke moves into cold shutdown.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) said Friday it had moved its 975 megawatt Indian Point 2 nuclear power plant from hot to cold shutdown, pushing back its restart to likely next week.
The unit, located at Indian Point, N.Y., went into a hot shutdown mode earlier this week in preparation for a restart which the company had said it expected also this week.
But as of early Friday, the unit had moved back into cold shutdown for valve repairs, said spokeswoman Joan Burger.
"When the repair is completed we will begin startup and again move into a hot shutdown mode," Burger said, adding electricity production from the unit would resume "probably next week."
Separately, the New York Power Authority's adjacent 965 megawatt Indian Point nuclear power unit 3 was operating at full capacity as of early Friday, the NRC said.
